drugs.moa: Blocks the stomach's proton pump, sharply reducing acid production.
adverse: Long-term: fractures, low magnesium, B12 deficiency, C. diff
nursing: Take before meals (30–60 min before breakfast)
Long-term use has risks — use lowest effective dose
teaching: Report black stools or trouble swallowing
drugs.tip: PPIs (-prazole): take before meals; long-term → fractures, low Mg²⁺, B12 deficiency, C. diff risk.

drugs.moa: Blocks serotonin receptors in the gut and brain to prevent nausea and vomiting.
drugs.tip: Ondansetron (-setron): antiemetic, watch QT prolongation. Give slow IV.

drugs.moa: Kills gram-positive bacteria (including MRSA) by disrupting cell-wall synthesis.
side: Infusion-related flushing if given too fast
adverse: Vancomycin infusion reaction ("red man") if rapid
nursing: Infuse slowly over at least 60 minutes to prevent flushing reaction
teaching: Report ringing in the ears or decreased urine output
drugs.tip: Vancomycin: nephro- + ototoxic, monitor trough & creatinine, infuse SLOW (≥60 min) to avoid flushing reaction.
drugs.pearl: **Slow the vanc** — rapid infusion causes the flushing ("red man") reaction.

drugs.moa: Relieves pain and reduces fever centrally; minimal anti-inflammatory effect.
nursing: Do not exceed the daily maximum (watch hidden acetaminophen in combo products)
Assess for liver disease and alcohol use
labs: Total daily dose from all sources
drugs.tip: Acetaminophen: max ~3–4 g/day, overdose → liver failure, antidote = acetylcysteine. Watch combo products.

drugs.moa: Blocks prostaglandins to relieve moderate pain and inflammation.
nursing: Assess renal function and for GI bleeding
teaching: Report black stools or stomach pain
drugs.tip: Ketorolac (NSAID): max 5 days, GI bleed + renal risk, take with food. Don't stack NSAIDs.
